content.value_statement: Email teams often lose subscribers when unsubscribe pages only offer a hard opt-out. This skill designs topic, cadence, pause, and suppression-rule choices that give subscribers lower-frequency options.
actual_capabilities: Defines preference-center fields for topics, cadence tiers, channel toggles, and save behavior.
Builds an ordered opt-down ladder before a hard unsubscribe path.
Maps each subscriber choice to an ESP suppression or frequency rule.
Produces a SEND N sub-item note for preference-center and frequency options.
Creates a handoff summary for consent registry and lifecycle-flow owners.
limitations: Does not compute the full email quality score or rule the unsubscribe veto.
Does not own the consent, opt-out, or suppression record of truth.
Does not design full lifecycle sequences or global cadence governance.
Requires user-provided topics, cadence tiers, or exports for measured accuracy.

use_cases.title: Reduce Hard Unsubscribes
use_cases.description: Create step-down choices that let subscribers reduce frequency, mute topics, or pause messages.

use_cases.title: Prepare Consent Handoffs
use_cases.description: Translate topic, cadence, and pause selections into suppression rules for registry review.

use_cases.title: Audit Preference Coverage
use_cases.description: Assess whether a preference center supports topic control, cadence control, pause options, and one-click opt-out.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Preference Center
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with known topics and a simple cadence set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a preference center for our newsletter. Topics are product updates, events, and weekly digest. Cadence options are weekly, monthly, and pause.

prompt_templates.title: Unsubscribe Opt-Down Ladder
prompt_templates.scenario: Offer alternatives before the subscriber leaves the list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an unsubscribe-page opt-down ladder for a SaaS audience. Include frequency reduction, topic selection, a 90-day pause, and the hard opt-out path.

prompt_templates.title: ESP Rule Mapping
prompt_templates.scenario: Connect preference choices to implementation rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Map each preference-center choice to ESP suppression or frequency rules for HubSpot. Include topic mutes, monthly cadence, and pause until a chosen date.

prompt_templates.title: N Sub-Item Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate preference-center readiness for an email quality audit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this preference center against the SEND N preference-center sub-item. Mark Pass, Partial, or Fail and explain the rule gaps to fix before audit.

output_examples.input: Build a preference center for product updates, events, and promotions with weekly and monthly cadence options.
output_examples.output: A field spec with three topic toggles, two cadence tiers, a pause option, save behavior, and clear confirmation text.

output_examples.input: Create an opt-down ladder for subscribers clicking unsubscribe after high campaign frequency.
output_examples.output: An ordered ladder that offers monthly cadence, topic selection, a 90-day pause, and then the one-click hard unsubscribe.

output_examples.input: Map our preference choices to consent and suppression rules.
output_examples.output: A rule mapping that sends topic mutes, cadence caps, pauses, and opt-outs to the appropriate registry and ESP controls.

best_practices: Keep the hard unsubscribe clear, reachable, and never hidden behind extra steps.
Offer only cadence tiers and topics that the email program can actually honor.
Label each source as measured, user-provided, or estimated in the handoff.
anti_patterns: Do not invent topic groups when the program sends no matching content stream.
Do not treat a pause option as consent to keep sending during the pause window.
Do not suppress the whole list when the subscriber only muted one topic.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a preference-center field spec, an opt-down ladder, a choice-to-rule mapping, and a SEND N sub-item note.

faq.question: Does it replace a consent registry?
faq.answer: No. It designs the mapping that a consent registry or ESP must record and honor.

faq.question: Can it design lifecycle email flows?
faq.answer: No. It references lifecycle cadence plans but does not design full email sequences or global send governance.

faq.question: What inputs improve the result?
faq.answer: Use topic lists, current cadence tiers, ESP preference exports, unsubscribe rates, and segment context when available.

faq.question: Does it block unsubscribes?
faq.answer: No. It requires the hard unsubscribe to stay clear and reachable while offering lower-frequency alternatives.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Email marketers, lifecycle leads, and marketing operations teams can use it to reduce fatigue while respecting preferences.
